title: Classical guitar
summary: One string is plucked at a time. Five of the six notes have only that string and no A or D string; the E4 page puts all six strings on the one bridge, E4 plucked and the other five ringing in sympathy. The body follows the plan of a 1964 Madrid guitar, not the recordings' Raimundo 118. The attack is too weak in the top octaves, E2 rings too long, and the body's low air tone dies away too slowly, and no cause is yet known. The nylon trebles and the wound E2 pluck a braced spruce top, African mahogany (Khaya) back and ribs at the 1.524 m listener, a rosewood bridge and the air inside, with a computed air load acting on the shell and sound hole. G3, B3, Gb4 and F5 also carry viscoelastic bending loss, air loading on the string and longitudinal string modes; E2 doesn't have the last two, and the six-string E4 page carries air loading on E4's string only and longitudinal modes on its three nylon strings, G3, B3 and E4. The renders are tuned to equal temperament and the recordings sit flat of it, so most of each pitch gap is the recordings'. The arpeggio and chord add separate renders, which don't exchange energy.
physics_present: The strings: nylon G3, B3 and E4 open, Gb4 and F5 stopped on the B string, and a wound E2 that takes its tension, line mass and bending stiffness whole from Woodhouse's 2004 measurement of one D'Addario set; on the E4 page the wound A2 and D3 from that set join E2, G3 and B3, all five at rest on the one bridge while E4 is plucked
Two polarizations on every string, with 48 bending modes per polarization on G3, 81 on B3, 60 on E4 (24 on each of the five strings at rest there), 24 on Gb4 and F5, and 96 on E2
Tension on the open trebles comes from tuning the model to equal temperament on an earlier card, so no recording sets a value. They sit within a few cents of it on these cards
The string modes above the kept set carry their exact static compliance into the bridge (residual flexibility)

On G3, B3, Gb4 and F5: viscoelastic bending loss from the pack's cited Kelvin-Voigt row, air loading on the string (cylinder-gas-loading 0.3 30 4) and longitudinal string modes (F5 takes the same nylon-b3 pack as B3 and Gb4, the one that carries that row); on the six-string E4 page the viscoelastic bending loss on the three nylon strings, air loading on E4's string only and axial modes on G3, B3 and E4, the wound E2, A2 and D3 transverse only (a measured whole string carries no axial stiffness), which the network admits at 983 complete modes under its 1024 ceiling
On E2: the friction and bending loss factors Woodhouse fitted to that string

The body of the 1964 Madrid guitar in Zimmer and Mores' 2024 plan: a braced Sitka spruce top with its sound hole, a barred African mahogany (Khaya) back, Khaya ribs and a rosewood bridge, with 128 body modes. On E2 the bridge's wall is drawn from the plan's own section (shell-assembly-h12-bridge-plan.tsv), whose lighter bridge moves the line read in the rendered sound, where the top's first mode couples with the air cavity, from 192.5 to 199.0 Hz (unloaded, before the cavity couples, from 149.6 to 157.9 Hz). The bridge mobility measured on this guitar (Mores 2021, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.4604577, g20: strongest line 198 Hz, air resonance A0 97 Hz; Mores' printed table gives 200 and 98 Hz) tests that reading: the plan-table body's cavity-coupled bridge mobility, read on a reduced card (the wound E2 string, a compact-neck cavity and no body-radiation skin, because the 128-mode body with the skin load does not fit the engine's 1024-unknown harmonic limit), has its strongest line at 203.6 Hz (+2.8 % against 198 Hz) and A0 at 95.2 Hz (-1.9 % against 97 Hz), so the 20 % gap between the unloaded 158 Hz line and the measured 198 Hz is the cavity coupling and not a structural miss. Above 230 Hz the unloaded structural lines of the drawn-table rosewood body, the specimen's wood, lie within -7 to +3 % of the measured ones (231 against 237 to 241, 255 against 269, 297 against 317, 408 against 410 and 500 to 513 against 506 Hz). Gb4, F5, G3, B3 and the six-string E4 page take the same section in a re-drawn table (shell-assembly-h12-bridge-plan-drawn.tsv; G3 comes to it from the first table's wall, 28.0 mm thick and 8.7 mm high) with the bridge where the specimen has it and the string force where its saddle is: the wall's centre is at 337.34 mm on the top, read from the plan's vector drawing of the bridge outline (182.8 by 28.8 mm as printed, +-0.1 mm; the front photograph agrees within +-1.4 mm), and the string force enters at the saddle, 9.67 mm toward the neck from the bridge's centre (the plan's printed saddle slot, 4.7 mm from the bridge's neck-side edge; 5.3 mm in the photograph), on a rigid massless arm. Disclosed: the arm has no mass and no flexibility, and the 22 mm wall is a line clamp in the model, so the top's rotational stiffness under the bridge is a line's. E2 keeps the earlier bridge at 334.54 mm, driven at its centre, until its page posts

Wood constants from the Wood Handbook (FPL-GTR-282), with wood loss measured on other samples: for the Khaya back and ribs the loss along the grain, eta_L = 0.0312 / pi, measured on Khaya ivorensis of another density (Laudares et al. 2023), and the other four loss factors a hardwood-median surrogate (Bremaud, Gril and Thibaut 2011)
A boundary-element air load on the shell and sound-hole port (body-radiation skin, 20-1100 Hz). It changes how the body moves, not how the note is picked up
The enclosed air with a radiating sound-hole neck, whose outer end takes its mass and radiation from that air load

On all six rendered notes: the sound hole's edge loss, an orifice-edge row on the exterior-neck cavity that adds the viscous loss at the hole's edge (Brandao and Schnitzer 2020, eq. 1.8-1.10), frozen at each card's own air-tone frequency. Resistance only: the equal reactance, about 0.6 % of the neck's air mass, is left out. It takes 3.3 to 3.6 dB off the air tone at 300 ms (3.6 on F5, Gb4 and E4, 3.5 on B3 and G3, 3.3 on E2); on E2 it also makes the fundamental decay about 0.14 dB/s faster through the body

A compact receiver at every frequency, on a 96 kHz clock, placed at 1.524 m: the UIowa guitar page's 5 feet in an anechoic chamber, the centre QTC40 of a Decca tree. The receiver is an exact 1/r on the cards tested (a 0.5 s Gb4 prefix at 1.524 m equals the 1 m prefix divided by 1.524 to within 0.824 LSB, the int16 rounding bound being 0.828, checked 8 November 2026; the E2 render at 1.524 m against its 1 m render divided by 1.524, 0.827 LSB over all 240000 samples, 9 November 2026), so a clip at 1 m is the same waveform scaled by 1.524

On E2 and Gb4: a spirit-shellac film on the outer face of the top, the back and both rib strips (not the bridge wall, the braces or the bars), 84 micrometres thick, with its storage modulus frozen at 1 kHz. Its law is the fit of Laemmlein et al. (2021) to dynamic mechanical analysis of a 1704-type spirit varnish, MEASURED ON VIOLIN SPECIMENS, not on a guitar (E0 70 MPa, Einf 1.89 GPa, alpha 0.330, beta 0.314, tau 0.125 s, density 984 kg/m3); the thickness is Stephens' (2015) sealer of 44 to 45 micrometres plus top coat of 39, measured on a 3 mm Sitka spruce bar, not on a guitar top. The Poisson ratio 0.30, the strain limit 0.001, the relative humidity 0.35 and the storage drift 0.25 are authored closures (no source gives a Poisson ratio)
physics_missing: The other strings: one sounds at a time, so nothing rings in sympathy, and A2 and D3 aren't rendered. The arpeggio and chord add posted clips, with no coupling through the bridge or body and a balance taken from each page's recording

The string modes above the kept set: partials stop at the 48th on G3, at the 81st on B3 and the 60th on E4 (the most the 96 kHz clock admits on each card; 82 on B3 is refused, and on the six-string E4 page 64, 68 and 70 are refused where 60 is admitted; one E4 string alone admits 70 and refuses 71), at the 24th on Gb4 and F5, and at the 96th on E2, which takes the top of the attack with them. On G3, B3 and E4 a faint line above the last partial isn't a partial: the kept modes move together on the bridge's flexibility, an artefact of the cut. The line moves with the cut: at 48 modes on G3 it sits at 11.3 kHz, 32 dB further under the fundamental in the first 100 ms than at 24 modes, and it's still most of what fills 8-16 kHz there. At 60 modes on E4 it sits at 23.1 kHz, above hearing, and at 81 modes on B3 it moves above hearing too, where it doesn't rise above the reader's floor, about 114 dB under the fundamental

Body modes above the 128 kept, and a converged body mesh. The body's resonances stop near 1770 Hz, and 2 kHz is the most the wood packs allow: their moduli come from the Wood Handbook's static values. A no-skin test with 148 modes moved the partials near the cut in both directions, and on Gb4 brought the octave closer through a partial the recording barely has, so more modes alone isn't a fix

The air tone's loss: the body's low air resonance dies away more slowly than the recording's on G3, B3, E4, Gb4 and F5. The hole's edge loss is on all six rendered notes; with it, over 50-160 ms, the recording's air tone still falls faster than the render's by about 34 dB/s on the B3 Khaya page, about 18 on the Gb4 film page and about 52 on the F5 Khaya page (each read on the page's own render with a 40 ms Hann window at the air line, 104 to 105 Hz in the recording and the card's 95.2 Hz in the render), and on E2 the air tone sits too close to the fundamental to read the recording's. On G3 and E4 the recording's air tone is under the noise by about 120 to 140 ms while the render's is still well above it. The computed air load on the outside (the skin) gives the air mode a Q about three times the older compact neck model's (78 against 24 on B3, where the recording implies about 37), as on the violin (52 against 19). On the violin the code read finds nothing dropped: the skin's full-space radiation is right and the compact end's half-space radiation was not, so the older, lower Q was partly wrong physics. On the guitar the skin keeps the compact end's flanged mass and puts back 0.61 of its resistance. What else damps the guitar's air mode isn't identified
G3's string: the recording's string is far less stiff than the printed nylon of this gauge, which suggests a different string; no print for it has been found

E2 is one measured set's whole-string coefficients, not its construction: the core and winding are unknown, and its diameter, which sets only its air drag, is a stand-in from another gauge. Its level falls far more slowly than the Iowa E2's on the posted clips. Longitudinal modes are refused on it: a measured whole string carries no axial stiffness, and no printed axial rigidity for the wound EJ46C string has turned up
The nylon's tension loss enters as zero, because the evidence table has no nylon row
The pluck: one point at one station, released from a static force, not measured on the recordings' player. No print gives the place on a stopped note. A finger or nail's width isn't modelled
Finger and fret contact on stopped notes (the fret is a rigid pinned end), and the player holding the guitar: the model hangs free

The string meets the body through an authored penalty spring (100000 N/m), not the saddle's contact mechanics. On Gb4, F5, G3, B3 and the six-string E4 page the spring acts at the saddle's point on the rigid arm; the second polarization's support (also 100000 N/m, along the body's -y) sits on the same wall triangle as the vertical drive, with the same weights and the same arm, on Gb4, F5, G3 and B3 and on each of the six strings of the E4 page, so its offset is zero there and a lateral force at the crest meets the wall through the arm

The body is one 1964 Madrid guitar's plan, not the Raimundo 118. The maker's pages print the 118's scale (650 mm) and its body depth (95 mm at the heel block, 100 mm at the tail), which agree with the plan's printed 94, 101 and 99 mm to about 1 mm; they print no outline, bracing, plate thickness or cedar species. The maker names the back and sides three ways in three dated captures: dyed mahogany (3 September 2011, three months before the recording session, with no word on laminate), dyed sapele (2018) and, in the shop listing of 2020, filed under laminated construction without saying which parts; the card plays African mahogany (Khaya) for the back and ribs, a choice, not the maker's word: stiffness and density are the Wood Handbook's Khaya, the loss along the grain is measured on Khaya ivorensis of another density, the other four loss factors are a hardwood-median surrogate, true mahogany (Swietenia) has only a loss factor ambiguous by a factor pi, and the plate is solid wood, no laminate is modelled. Each part has one thickness. The neck and heel, blocks, linings, rosette, fingerboard, bridge patch, string holes, back strip and patches, glue and finish are left out

The plan names no bridge wood: rosewood is assumed. It prints no bridge position either: Gb4, F5, G3, B3 and the six-string E4 page read it from the plan's drawn outline of the bridge and the photograph, and E2 still uses a station inferred from the gap between the plan's axis strips, 2.8 mm nearer the neck than the drawn one

The air load stops at 1100 Hz, and the receiver is compact at every frequency, not a boundary-element microphone. UIowa's own pages disagree with its guitar page, and the card does not resolve it: the microphone inventory lists only QTC50s where the guitar page says QTC40, and the post-2012 page gives 24-bit at 44.1 kHz where the guitar page gives 24-bit at 96 kHz

The loaded harmonic response of the coupled performer (the bridge mobility with the strings, cavity and exterior reaction in it) cannot be exported for these cards: the engine admits at most 1024 coordinates plus poles for it (MAX_HARMONIC_UNKNOWNS), and the G3 card is refused at that check after about 190 s, both in full and with its string cut from 48 to 6 modes and its gas and axial rows removed. Only the unloaded structural mobility, which has no strings, cavity or exterior reaction, can be read
Geometric stretching of the string isn't enabled: it's an alternative to the longitudinal waves, with no published coefficient
The output is 16-bit at a full scale of 1 Pa, so the quietest top-band content sits at the quantisation floor

The finish: only the E2 and Gb4 pages carry a varnish, a spirit-shellac film whose numbers come from violin specimens and a spruce bar, not from a guitar. A hunt on 9 November 2026 found no measured modulus, loss or thickness of a French-polish film on a guitar. As a check outside the pages' own numbers, the same law on Stephens' (2015) Sitka spruce bars predicts +4.8 Hz across the grain and -6.2 Hz along it, against +5 to +7 and -7 to -11 Hz measured after seven weeks' cure. The F5 page carries no film: a trial (Laemmlein et al. 2021, 84 micrometres, storage frozen at 1 kHz) moved the fundamental by 0.1 cent and made the first second 1.0 to 1.7 dB quieter, and in the grader's read took the page from 10 to 9 measures inside the ruler, the decay measure leaving it (67.34 dB/s against a ruler maximum of 67.14)
